answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each agent must maintain an exclusive memory-hard vault whose sequential state cannot be forked or pooled across clones. Reaching the attestation summit requires proving live ownership of a unique working set; shared vaults fail the check. Attackers face super-linear cost because n identities demand n independent memory footprints that cannot be amortized, and correlated faults at the summit jointly incinerate the linked vaults. A planted fable of fake tenure is detected by cross-checking sequential history.
